chunks: I heard al-Reza (peace be upon him) saying:
'The servant cannot happen to be (any) closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than when he is performing sajdah,
and that is the Words of the Mighty and Majestic: 'And make obeisance and get closer (to Allah)' [96:19].'

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ: al-abd — the servant/slave of God, denoting human dependence on Allah
key_terms.سَاجِدٌ: sajid — one who is in prostration (sajdah)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: 'azza wa jall — 'Mighty and Majestic', an honorific for Allah

ai.seo_question: When is a Muslim closest to Allah according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) teaches that the moment of sajdah (prostration) is when the believer is nearest to Allah, supporting this with the Quranic command in Surah al-Alaq (96:19). This teaching, transmitted by al-Washsha who heard it directly from the Imam, emphasizes the spiritual significance of the prostration position in salat. For the early community of believers, this saying provided a profound theological motivation for sincere and attentive prostration during prayer.
